contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, schema, shared volumes
Output records: verified, rejected, merge.hold, merge.hold.lifted
Mechanism: verify-main.sh lifted into the Go service, with the hold as a record
How it starts without an agent typing

pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.sentence: When the full suite set has run on a main sha after a merge, the Go service writes verified 201 for every pull request the sha carries since the last verified sha, or rejected 422 naming the sha and the red suites plus one merge.hold record that stops every merge until a later main is green, and no seat is involved.
purpose.is: The verify loop of the three loops (AGENTS.md Law: three loops, always): merged to verified or held, scripted, non-disruptive.

The answer to C42's question "who verifies main": the system does, as code reading coq/gate on the main sha (D05, D11); the merger seat (C18) and the architect (SPEC-17 n-verify, S1-023) are retired from it.
The hold is a record in the one store (D10), read by N-09 before and during every merge, shown on the Alerts and Controls screens, and lifted only by a green main or an owner break glass.
purpose.is-not: Not a suite runner: N-26 runs the suites as pods and posts coq/gate on the main sha; this node reads the result.
Not a revert: a red main is fixed forward by a fix ticket (dag.md section 4 re-entry at N-03); a revert is rejected with reason below.
purpose.decisions: D05 (C43), D10 (C34), D11 (C39), D15 (C50), V03 (hold file pattern, now a record), roadmap ruling 2026-10-13T19:41Z (verify coalesce).

record.field: The main sha the full suite set ran on (N-04's snapshot carries the raw status as main_gate; N-26 turns it into this record with the suites and the merge_seq).
The merge_seq of the merge record whose merge_sha equals main_sha (N-26 copies it); the order key.
success, failure or error (after N-24's ladder and N-25's three posts).
Every suite with its exit code and log url; every suite runs even after one fails (verify-main.sh choice 1).

Set with code 410 when the run was coalesced away for a newer main sha (abortPrevious); state is error, this node writes nothing and the newer sha's status covers this range. With N-09's awaiting-verify step this happens only after a push outside the line.

input.reads: Merge records ordered by merge_seq; the newest verified record; the current merge.hold record; the halt record; the newest protection.observed and protection.drift (N-04), which assert linear history on main.
input.starts-when: A main.gate.status record is committed; the scheduler tick also re-examines any merge record older than verify.expected_seconds (d-verify of shared/retry-budget.xml#deadlines: N-26's run bound d-main-run plus the poll and 600 s) with no main.gate.status, and writes main.verify.missing 500 once (see waits).

record.field: N-10/verified/<pr>@<merge_sha>/r1; one per pull request, ever.
The green main sha and the range of merge_seq it covers (coalescing: a green main verifies every merge since the last verified).
record.rule: verified is the trigger of everything that acts on main being good: N-03 moves the ticket merged to done (shared/contracts.xml#ticket-transitions), N-35 deploys the map, N-47 publishes the book and N-48 promotes stable, each reading the merge record's paths by merge_sha; none acts on a merge record alone (F13).

record.field: N-10/rejected/<main_sha>/r1; one per red sha (verify-main.sh choice 2: the sha is red, not a pull request).
Every pull request in the range, each with its ticket; the fix ticket names them.
The failing suites with their log urls.
1 to 3: how many fix tickets this hold has spawned.

field.name: held_sha, held_merge_seq, reason, prs, suites_red, rejected_id

record.field: false until a merge.hold.lifted names it; N-09 reads the newest hold and merges only when it is lifted.
by is green-main with the green sha, or break-glass with the control.action id.
A merge with no main.gate.status past the bound; once per merge.

output.ends-when: Every merge in the range has a verified record, or the rejected and merge.hold records exist and the fix re-entry was written; a superseded status ends with no record.

mechanism.where: Go package verify inside the service; a port of line/bin/verify-main.sh's verdict and hold logic, with the suites moved to pods (N-26) and the hold moved from a file to a record.
mechanism.step: Load the main.gate.status and its merge_seq; a 410 (superseded_by set) ends here with no record. Load the newest verified record's merge_seq (last_verified). The range is last_verified plus 1 to this merge_seq, as merge records. A status whose merge_seq is at or below last_verified is stale (an older run finishing late, verify-main.sh choice 3) and ends with no record.

A status with superseded_by set ends with no record: the newer sha's status covers the range (ci/README.md abortPrevious; roadmap ruling 19:41Z: verify only the newest main sha, drop queued older runs).

state success: for each merge record in the range write verified 201 (key pr:merge_sha). Then, if a merge.hold stands whose held_merge_seq is at or below this merge_seq, write merge.hold.lifted by green-main and compare-and-swap the hold's lifted field to true; an older green never lifts a newer red (verify-main.sh choice 3, with merge_seq in place of git ancestry because main has required linear history). Linear history is asserted, not assumed: merge_seq ordering is used only while the newest protection.observed (N-04, shared/authority.xml#github-app) says linear history is on and no protection.drift is newer; otherwise a green verifies only the merges N-26 listed by ancestry and lifts no hold, and a red is rejected with reason linear-history-unverified, so the safe side is the hold.

state failure, or error after N-25's three posts: write rejected 422 for the sha with every pull request in the range and the red suites; write merge.hold 423 unless a hold already stands (the first red holds; a second red while held updates nothing, because the hold is a fact until green). fix_attempt is the count of rejected records since the last verified plus one.

Re-entry: with fix_attempt at or below 3, write a ticket.request (reason fix-for-hold, rejected_id, hold_id, request id fix-<hold_id>-<fix_attempt>) to N-03, which admits it as a cut request CR-<request id> at phase spec (nodes/N-03/spec.xml#input); N-02 leases it and N-07 dispatches a spec-author run (N-17) whose brief is the rejected record and the red logs, N-18 validates its fix ticket on main, N-03 readies it, and the normal worker, gate, review, merge path runs; the hold stands throughout, so the fix pull request's merge is the only merge N-09 allows under a hold (hold exception, ../N-09/spec.xml#m-hold: the fix ticket entity carries hold_id equal to the standing hold's hold_id, set by N-03 when it admits the ticket set cut from this request, and N-09's merge record carries fix_for_hold_id). With fix_attempt 4 the hold stays, no new fix is cut, and the rejected record maps to owner-acts so N-28 posts exactly one card with the sha, the suites, the three fix tickets and the recommendation.

A main.gate.status whose main_sha matches no merge record (a hand push to main, a merge by hand) is written as rejected with reason unknown-sha and a hold: fail closed (verify-main.sh hold choice 1: the file existing is the hold whatever it holds). The card tells the owner what landed outside the line (D19 exit test counts it as an agent line operation if a seat did it).
mechanism.invariant: The newest merge.hold decides: N-09 reads the newest hold record and its lifted flag; a lift is a separate record plus a compare-and-swap, so the history is append-only.
verified is written once per pull request and never for a range that a red sha covers.
mechanism.diagram: flowchart TD S["main.gate.status on main sha M (merge_seq k)"] --> O{"k above last verified?"} O -- no --> E0["stale, end"] O -- yes --> SU{"superseded_by set?"} SU -- yes --> E0 SU -- no --> ST{"state"} ST -- success --> V["verified 201 per PR in range"] V --> HL{"hold with held_seq at or below k?"} HL -- yes --> LF["merge.hold.lifted by green-main"] HL -- no --> E1["end"] ST -- "failure or error" --> R["rejected 422 for M, prs, red suites"] R --> H["merge.hold 423 (unless one stands)"] H --> FA{"fix_attempt at or below 3?"} FA -- yes --> FX["ticket.request fix-for-hold: N-03 cut request, spec-author cuts the fix ticket (N-17, N-18, N-03)"] FA -- no --> CARD["owner-acts: one card by N-28"] FX --> E1 LF --> E1

start.sentence: Nothing here starts by an agent typing.
start.by: N-26 starts a Jenkins run on every merge record and posts coq/gate on the main sha (N-25); N-04 polls it into a snapshot; N-26 writes main.gate.status; its commit starts this node. The scheduler tick re-examines merges with no status past the bound.
start.restart: After a crash the next main.gate.status re-derives the range from merge_seq and last_verified; nothing is remembered in memory. A hold survives a restart because it is a record.
start.never: No seat verifies main; no architect checks a 201 against acceptance criteria (L13 section 7 D03: 66 verified posted by an LLM, median 28 minutes after merge).

wait.timeout: verify.expected_seconds, d-verify of shared/retry-budget.xml#deadlines (N-26's run bound d-main-run plus the poll plus 600 s), so a run inside its own bound is never reported missing
wait.fallback: main.verify.missing 500 once per merge to N-41 and N-28; the hold is not written, because the absence of a verdict is a system-lane fault, not a red main; N-09 keeps every other merge held awaiting-verify meanwhile (fail closed)

wait.on: N-01 read of merges, verified, hold
wait.fallback: end the traversal; the next status or tick retries; three in a row write store.unreachable 500 once

wait.on: N-01 writes of verified, rejected, hold, lifted
wait.fallback: retry 1 s, 2 s, 4 s; then verify.write.failed 500 once per main_sha; the next traversal re-derives and rewrites (keys make it idempotent)

wait.on: a fix ticket turning main green
wait.timeout: 3 fix attempts (N-11's count applies inside each ticket; this node counts tickets)
wait.fallback: one owner card with the recommendation; the hold stands; product work is frozen by D19 in any case

waits.rule: No sleep and no git call in this node: ordering uses merge_seq, which N-01 mints in the merge transaction.

step.name: record write
step.then: verify.write.failed 500 once per sha; re-derived next traversal

step.name: red main fix
step.backoff: none; each fix is a full ticket traversal
step.then: rejected record maps to owner-acts; N-28 one card; the hold stands

retries.not-retried: A red suite is never re-run by this node to see if it goes green (V05: an assertion failure is never retried); flaky suites are a system-lane ticket from the fix path.
retries.report: Every then clause is a record; the owner sees a red main as one card with the fix history, never as a stream.

many-agents.readers: Any number of seats read verified and rejected records; a fix spec-author brief cites the rejected id; every merge traversal (N-09) reads the newest hold.
many-agents.two-statuses: Two main.gate.status records in flight (a slow suite set finishing after a newer one): merge_seq ordering makes the older one stale or superseded, so an old green never lifts a new red and an old red never holds after a newer green (verify-main.sh choice 3).
many-agents.two-holds: Two traversals that both see a red sha both try merge.hold main_sha:hold; the idempotency key makes the second a 409 that is logged; the lifted compare-and-swap refuses a second lift on the same generation.
many-agents.hold-versus-merge: N-09 reads the newest hold twice per merge (before and right before the merge call); a hold written in the remaining window of milliseconds cannot stop that one merge, which is why the fix path and the required check on main both exist (merge.sh hold choice 2). The merge that slipped is in the next range and verifies or rejects with it.
many-agents.fix-under-hold: Many fix tickets are not cut for one red sha: the ticket.request is keyed by hold id and fix attempt, so a second traversal replays it (200) instead of a second request, and N-03 refuses a second fix ticket naming the same hold until the first is verified or dead.
many-agents.conflict-reports: Every 409 and every refused compare-and-swap is logged with the key and counted; never a silent overwrite.
many-agents.test: Test case old-green-new-red: statuses for seq 5 (red) and seq 4 (green) arriving in either order leave the hold standing (checklist c-order).

emits.acts: N-03 admits it as a spec-phase cut request (fix-for-hold)
N-51 exit test counts it; N-45 retention clock starts; the owner's done line through N-28's rule
N-03 admits the ticket.request for the fix (attempts 1 to 3); owner-acts at fix_attempt 4 (N-28 one card); N-41
N-09 merges nothing but the fix; N-41 and N-42 show it

reads.acts: verdicts are still written under halt, because a verdict is a fact; the fix lease request waits for resume

state-paths.root: $COQ_STATE as in ../N-07/spec.xml#state-paths; path elements in N-45's generator form.
state-paths.path: Rows: verified, rejected, merge.hold, merge.hold.lifted, main.verify.missing. A standing hold is never pruned; lifted holds and verified records prune after retention (N-01's row).
One line per step with the range and the suites; suite logs themselves are N-24's paths.
state-paths.never: No merge-hold.json file (rejected item 1); no verify worktree (rejected item 2); no file under the repository.

permissions.reads: main.gate.status, merge, verified, merge.hold, halt, ruling (break glass) records.
permissions.writes: verified, rejected, merge.hold, merge.hold.lifted, main.verify.missing, verify.write.failed, store.unreachable records; the ticket.request for a fix; the verify log.
permissions.never: No suite run, no pod, no GitHub call, no git, no revert, no pane, no edit of any record except the compare-and-swap of the hold's lifted field, which is the one mutable field and carries its generation.
permissions.seat: No seat can write verified, rejected or merge.hold (N-01 writer identity); the fix spec-author seat reads the rejected record through its brief.

gauge.name: hold_age_seconds
gauge.from: now minus the standing hold's at

gauge.name: verify_lag_seconds
gauge.from: newest merge at minus its verified at, per merge

lamp.red: a hold stands or main.verify.missing open

alert.to: N-41 at once; one card at fix_attempt 4

runbook.bring-up: N-26 posting main.gate.status; set verify.enabled true; proof: a verified record for the newest merge whose main_sha equals origin/main.
runbook.read-status: Scheduler.Status shows last_verified, unverified merges, the standing hold with its sha, age and fix attempts; the Alerts screen shows the same; the Controls screen shows the HOLD lamp.
runbook.red-main: Nothing by hand: the fix ticket is cut by the spec-author run, the hold lets only that fix merge, a green main lifts the hold. After three fixes the card asks the owner.
runbook.break-glass-lift: The owner lifts a hold from the Controls screen (N-42, one time, recorded by N-29 as a ruling); this node writes merge.hold.lifted by break-glass with the ruling id. Never a hand delete of a record.
runbook.recover-missing: N-26 runbook re-requests the run; this node writes verified when the status lands.
runbook.registry: Generated into shared/cleanup-registry.json from the state-paths element (../N-45/spec.xml#state-paths).

merges are serialised by N-09 and N-26 runs per merge, so a red range is normally one merge; when a range is longer because runs were superseded, the rejected record lists every pull request and the fix ticket's spec-author reads the red logs. A bisect would re-run suites on intermediate shas, which V05 forbids as a retry of assertions and which costs pods; it is listed here so the ruling is not lost.
